description.summary: per-surface glass item hints for riode-glass

protocol.description:
A riode-glass-specific extension. It lets a client describe how the riode-glass compositor plugin should render the backdrop effect it applies to any surface that also carries an ext-background-effect-v1 blur region: the raw liquid-glass material (exact engine bytes) and what rounded-rect shape to clip the effect to.
This protocol only ever provides hints. A compositor without the riode-glass plugin loaded, or one that unloads it, has no obligation to honor any request here, and every object created by this protocol keeps working (as a silent no-op) rather than becoming a protocol error, precisely so that hint state never has to be treated as load-bearing by a client.
Shape of the protocol follows hyprglass-item-v1 (genericized), with the preset-name channel replaced by raw material bytes: client and plugin speak the same `Glass` language, no names anywhere.

interface.name: riode_item_manager_v1

description.summary: manager to associate glass item hints with surfaces

interface.description:
This is a Hyprland-riode-glass-specific extension. It lets a client hint how the riode-glass compositor plugin should render the effect it applies to any surface that also carries an ext-background-effect-v1 blur region: the raw glass material, and what rounded-rect shape to clip the effect to.
This protocol only ever provides hints. A compositor without the riode-glass plugin loaded, or one that unloads it, has no obligation to honor any request here, and every object created by this protocol keeps working (as a silent no-op) rather than becoming a protocol error, precisely so that hint state never has to be treated as load-bearing by a client.

request.name: destroy
request.description: This does not affect any riode_item_v1 objects already created.

request.name: get_item

description.summary: create a glass item hint object for a surface

request.description:
Create a riode_item_v1 object for the given wl_surface. Only one active (non-inert) such object may exist per surface at a time; creating a second one for the same surface while the first is still active raises the item_exists error. Inert objects left over from a previous manager global do not count.
This request does not, by itself, cause the surface to receive any effect: the effect is still gated on the surface itself carrying an ext-background-effect-v1 blur region. The object created here only supplies hints used when that effect is drawn.

event.name: finished
event.description: Sent when the compositor is about to make this global permanently unusable, for example because the riode-glass plugin is being unloaded. The client should stop issuing new requests on this manager and any riode_item_v1 objects it created; it does not have to destroy them, since they are guaranteed to remain valid, inert objects rather than become protocol errors.

entry.name: item_exists
entry.summary: the surface already has a riode_item_v1 object

interface.name: riode_item_v1

description.summary: glass rendering hints for one surface

interface.description: Carries optional per-surface hints for the riode-glass effect: the raw liquid-glass material, and what rounded-rect shape to clip the effect to. The two hints are independent: either can be set without the other. None of these requests raises an error for an out-of-range value; being hints, invalid values are ignored or clamped as described per request. All state is double-buffered per wl_surface.commit.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroying this object clears the surface's association with it.

request.name: set_glass
request.description: Sets the pending material: the packed glass frame as little-endian u32 words — version tag 5, frame blur sigma x/y (device px), integer sample box x0, y0, w, h (device px, used verbatim for blit/scissor/uSize; shape rects in the floats are box-relative), then the 792 uniform floats the optics shader consumes directly (the 736-float prefix plus the 56-float glow tail: count/dpr/light, per-shape rects/radii/variants/tints, the 36 variant-constant vec4s, group/extra/clip/blur arrays, glow/blend tail). 799 words exactly; any other size or version is ignored (unset behavior — the plain-blur fallback applies). The client packs (`pack_glass_wire`); the plugin uploads blindly, so there is one source of truth and no C++ pack to drift. There are no preset names. Version history: 1 was the P1 30-float material (retired with the P1 port); 2/3 were engine-internal and never consumed; 4 was the 736-float prefix wire; 5 adds the 56-float glow tail.

arg.name: material
arg.summary: v5 packed glass frame: version + sigma + box + 792 floats, LE u32s

request.name: unset_glass
request.description: Reverts to the compositor's plain-blur fallback for the surface's blur region.

request.name: set_shape

description.summary: hint an explicit rounded-rect clip shape

request.description: Sets the pending shape: a rectangle in surface-local logical coordinates, with up to four independent corner radii, that the effect is clipped and shaped to. If w or h is zero or negative, the shape is ignored (unset behavior). A negative radius is treated as zero. Radii are clamped the same way as CSS border-radius.

request.name: unset_shape
request.description: Reverts to the compositor's normal shape fallback: the extents of the surface's ext-background-effect-v1 blur region.

request.name: set_effect

description.summary: describe one custom effect stage in the ordered stack

request.description: Sets one pending custom effect stage: its position in the layer's ordered effect stack (`stack_index`, the absolute index over ALL stages — the glass stage included), the complete WGSL module implementing the effect ABI (the client prepends the ABI definitions; the module defines exactly `fn apply(...) -> EffectCtx` plus any helpers it needs), packed little-endian f32 uniforms (whole vec4s only), which backdrop texture the stage reads (`backdrop_need`), and that backdrop's blur sigma in device px (`backdrop_sigma`, meaningful for `read_blurred` only; 0 elsewhere). Indices may arrive in any order; the executor sorts by index. A duplicate index replaces the earlier pending stage at that index. The whole set is cleared by `clear_effects`, which the client sends at the head of every commit's batch, so a shrinking stack can never leak stale stages across commits. Out-of-range or misaligned payloads are ignored per-request — hints never raise protocol errors.

arg.name: stack_index
arg.summary: absolute position among all stages, bottom to top

arg.name: wgsl
arg.summary: complete WGSL module: ABI header (client-prepended) + apply definition

arg.name: uniforms
arg.summary: packed f32 uniforms, LE bytes, whole vec4s

arg.name: backdrop_sigma
arg.summary: ReadBlurred sigma, device px (0 when unused)

request.name: clear_effects

description.summary: clear all pending custom effect stages

request.description: Drops every pending effect stage for the next commit's apply. Sent at the head of each commit's batch so the latched set always mirrors the current stack exactly.

request.name: set_glass_stage

description.summary: position of the glass frame within the ordered stack

request.description: Sets the pending stack index of the glass frame (`set_glass`) among all stages: -1 when the stack carries no glass stage (every latched stage is a plain backdrop stage). Values below -1 clamp to -1; an omitted request keeps the previous value. Sent every commit alongside `clear_effects`, so the position tracks stack edits (moving Glass, then Glass at the bottom).
